MEMORANDUM

  Agenda Item #: _5_
  Meeting Date: January 15, 2020

TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL

THRU:  KENNETH RUKAVINA, ACTING CITY MANAGER

FROM:  CARL MORITZ, URBAN FORESTER

SUBJECT: CONSIDERATION OF PARKLANDS COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATIONS OF
  NOVEMBER 14, 2019

DATE:  JANUARY 15, 2020

Issue/Purpose

The purpose of this memorandum is to transmit Parklands Committee recommendation for applications
from the November 14, 2019 meeting to the City Council.

Background/Discussion

At its meeting of November 14, 2019, the Parklands Committee reviewed and discussed three
applications for change of the designated street tree, one application for both tree removal and removal
of non-native shrubs and trees in Parklands and an ad hoc committee report to address parkland
encroachments.

1.  PC-523-19; Application for change of the designated street tree adjacent to 3701 Via Valmonte

  Applicant:  Marlene Breene
  2325 Palos Verdes Drive West # 212
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff indicated the application was for change of the designated street tree adjacent to 3701 Via Valmonte,
to match the existing Olive tree by planting another Olive tree. Staff noted the existing Olive tree was in
very poor health and the prognoses was for the tree to continue to deteriorate without improving in
appearance. Most importantly, the neighborhood character is uniformly represented the entire length of

  1
  001
 the street by the designated street tree, the Peruvian pepper, and this is the only Olive tree on Via
Valmonte.

The applicant’s representative, Marlene Breene, indicated she was not aware of the condition of the tree
but the owners of the home would prefer no tree if the Olive is denied to plant and the Peruvian pepper
is required. The new landscape was designed as a Mediterranean garden and the peppers are not
compatible with the plant palette.

The committee members agreed the neighborhood character is strongly Peruvian peppers and were
reluctant to set a precedent. The Eucalyptus nicholii (Willow leafed Peppermint Gum) is the designated
street tree for Paseo Del Campo. Due to the location of this home being on the corner of Paseo Del Campo
and Via Valmonte, the designated street tree of Paseo Del Campo could be an option.

Action: Committee member Jeff Groves motioned second by Robert Cooper to recommend to the
City Council approval to plant either the designated street tree for Via Valmonte or Paseo Del
Campo The vote was (4-0-1, in favor, Richie-Bray dissenting).

2.  PC-524-19; Application to remove 3 London Plane trees and change of the designated street tree
  adjacent to 2825 Via Neve

  Applicant:  Deborah Richie-Bray
  2432 Via Amador
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Action: Committee member Groves motioned seconded by Cooper to recommend continuing the
application to the following meeting to allow an appropriate path to be chosen with all the
considerations to avoid any perceived conflict of interest. The vote was (4-0-1, in favor, Richie-Bray
recused).

3.  PC-525-19; Application for a change of the designated street tree adjacent to 4008 Via
  Largavista

  Applicant:  Allan Rigg
  6903 Cherty Drive
  Rancho Palos Verdes, CA 90275

Staff indicated this application for change of the designated street tree adjacent to 4008 Via Largavista
was to enable the two Olive trees planted partially in the parkway to stay in their present location. All site
plans, including the landscape plan submitted to the Palos Verdes Homeowners Association indicted the
trees were on private property and no plan was submitted to the City.

The policy for designating street trees to create visual unity and continuity in the streetscape as well as
contributing to the overall beauty of the community, the existing neighborhood character, how and why
the designated street tree could be changed, difficulties in managing mutually owned trees and the options
available to the committee were presented by staff.

The applicant provided a number of reasons to approve the trees including an honest mistake was made
by the Landscape Architect, confusion of the installing contractor with multiple plans, other unpermitted
olives existing on the street, larger size trees than required adding beauty to the neighborhood and the

  2
  002
 designated street tree not being an appropriate choice due to the aggressive characteristics of the root
system.

The Committee was sympathetic but concerned about not violating the designated street tree policy. A
majority of the committee didn’t want to set a precedent to change the designated street tree due to a
contractor’s mistake. The committee also understood the option to relocate the trees was viable and would
solve the problems created by mutually owned trees.

Action: Committee member Cooper motioned second by Groves to recommend denial to the City
Council and require the Olive trees to be removed from the public parkway. The vote was (4-1, in
favor, Richie-Bray dissenting).

4.  PC-527-19; Application for a change of the designated street tree adjacent to 2101
  Chelsea Road

  Applicant:  Kirby Larson
  2101 Chelsea Road
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

Staff introduced this application as a change of the designated street tree from the Australian Willow to
an Olive tree. Olive trees were planted in the private landscape and the homeowners prefer the Olive if
they are required to plant street trees. The planting of Australian Willows has only occurred where new
homes were required by the conditions contained in Neighborhood Compatibility applications. The
neighborhood character is not well defined yet and only six Australian Willows have been planted. Staff
suggested reducing the number of trees required to plant and provided an optional small scale tree to
consider if planting more Olive trees is denied.

The applicant indicated changes were required by the Planning Commission for their neighbor’s view
concerns. The applicant believes the Australian Willows are not compatible with the neighborhood and
the trees would completely obscure the view of the home and restrict their neighbor’s view corridor. They
agreed the Forest Pansy trees would look good with their landscape as an option for the street tree
requirements.

The Committee discussed the tree options relative to view impacts, neighborhood character, number of
trees required and the designated street tree policy. After reviewing the options, the Committee agreed
that three Eastern Redbud Forest Pansy trees were the best option and changing the designated street tree
for the rest of the street may be a future consideration.

Action: Committee member Richie-Bray motioned second by Cooper to recommend to the City
Council approval to plant three non-designated street trees, the Eastern Redbud ‘Forest Pansy’,
adjacent to 2101 Chelsea Road. The vote was (5-0).

5.  PC-528-19; Application to remove all trees and non-native shrubs located in the parkway and
  Parklands adjacent to 1400 Chelsea Road

  Applicant:  Marlene Breene
  2325 Palos Verdes Drive West, #212
  Palos Verdes Estates, CA 90274

  3
  003
 The application requested removal of one Chinese Flame tree, which is the designated street tree for this
portion of Chelsea Road, and also requested the removal of all non-native shrubs and trees in the adjacent
parklands called the Margate Parkway. The reasons for the application was view enhancement of the
ocean by removal of the Chinese Flame tree and improvement of the natural look of the Parklands by
removal of invasive ornamental plants. Staff noted the Chinese Flame tree was planted a long time ago
before it was the designated street tree and is in the middle of the view. It has been topped regularly over
the years without approval from the City by the previous resident. Staff indicated that a follow up
application to plant native plants in the subject area may follow but a minimum of mulch and removal of
all stumps of the plants removed would be required.

The applicant’s representative, Marlene Breene, indicated the area has been neglected for years.
Additionally, the city will benefit from her client’s generosity to clean-up the area and remove the
encroachments in Parklands. She indicated her client is willing to restore the area with natives after the
removals.

The Committee was in agreement with the concept to clean up the encroachments in Parklands but were
concerned about the restoration options and/or requirements. All committee members had input and
discussed the options. They all agreed it would be a benefit to remove all the non-native shrubs and trees
in the Parklands adjacent to 1400 Via Montemar. One member preferred to keep the Chinese Flame tree
until after the cleanup and a better evaluation of the area could be made.

Action: Committee member Cooper motioned second by Groves to recommend approval to the
City Council to remove all trees and non-native shrubs in the parkway and Parklands adjacent to
1400 Chelsea Road according to the ‘Standard Conditions For Tree Removal Approvals’. Require
$500 payment to the ‘Tree Bank’, removal of all stumps and placement of mulch in the affected
area. The vote was (4-1, in favor, Richie-Bray dissenting).

6.  Encroachments Ad Hoc Committee Report

Staff and Ad Hoc Committee Members presented an update to committee members on the progress by
the Ad Hoc Committee. The purpose of the report was intended to invite comment from the other
members of the committee and members of the public.

Three recommendation were made for consideration.

  1. Increase fines to motivate compliance.
  2. Consider an initial one-year program without fines to abate encroachments voluntarily.
  3. Determine administrative costs (Code Enforcement Officer on staff or a Consultant).

The Ad Hoc Committee will reconvene and consider these recommendations and then return at a
subsequent Parklands Committee with their recommendations for updating the Parklands Encroachment
Abatement Policy.

Notification

Interested parties attending the Parklands Committee meeting were made aware that the above noted
recommendations would be transmitted to the City Council. This item is also noticed in the standard
manner for City Council meetings.

  4
  004
 Alternatives Available to the City Council

City Council has the option to approve, deny, amend or remand this item to the Parklands Committee.
Should the City Council consider amending and have its own hearing on this item, it is recommended
that the discussion be calendared for a future meeting so appropriate notice can be assured.

Recommendation

It is recommended that the City Council review and approve the Parklands Committee recommended
actions of November 14, 2019.

B. Staff report for PC-524-19
C. Staff report for PC-525-19
D. Staff report for PC-527-19
E. Staff report for PC-528-19
